chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I was sitting in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) at the door of his house in Medina, so he looked at the people passing by in droves. He said to one of those present: 'Has an event occurred in Medina?' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! A governor has been appointed over Medina, so the people are going in the morning to congratulate him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The man is fed with the matter to be congratulated for, and indeed it is a door from the doors of the Fire.'

key_terms.وُلِّيَ: appointed to a position of authority

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the spiritual status of a newly appointed governor?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) contextualizes the appointment of secular rulers by observing the public's celebratory reaction to a new governor, contrasting worldly honor with spiritual peril. He identifies the office not merely as a duty but as a 'door to the Fire,' a concept deeply rooted in Shia political theology that warns of the inherent corruption and distraction from divine accountability when authority is sought or bestowed for status. This highlights the critical Shia distinction between the Imamate's divinely ordained leadership and the often transient, potentially corrupt nature of temporal political power.

en.hubeali: Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I was seated in the presence of Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> at the door of his<sup>asws</sup> house at Al-Medina, so he<sup>asws</sup> looked at the people passing by in droves. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to someone in his<sup>asws</sup> presence: ‘Has an event occurred in Al-Medina?’ So he said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! A (new) governor has been appointed, so the people are attending lunch to welcome him’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The man is feeding for a matter to be congratulated by, and he is at the door from doors of the Fire’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ibn abu ‘Umayr has narrated from Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following: “

I once was sitting in the presence of abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, near the door of his house and he (the Imam) looked at the people passing in throngs and mobs. He (the Imam) asked someone near him, ‘Has anything happened in al-Madinah?’ He replied, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, a new governor is assigned for al-Madinah and people are served lunch to welcome and congratulate him.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘The man serves people lunch to receive their congratulation and he is a door of the doors of the fire.’”
